acme-devops: Hey @Lina — after we rolled out a strict deny-all egress NetworkPolicy in our `prod` namespace, our Redwood Private agent pods started reporting TLS handshake failures when calling the control plane. API requests are 503ing. Logs attached below.

Lina (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, we'll triage. Can you paste the exact NetworkPolicy you applied and a short `kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -o wide` + `kubectl -n prod get networkpolicy`? Also any pod logs from `redwood-agent` showing the TLS errors.

acme-devops: Thanks — here's the NP we applied in `prod` (deny all egress):

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-all
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```

and a snippet from `redwood-agent` logs: 
```
2026-03-12T14:02:10Z error tls: handshake failure while dialing https://controller.redwood.internal:443
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z warn dial tcp 10.42.5.3:443: i/o timeout
```

Lina (Support): Ok. Two quick things we usually see: (1) NetworkPolicy was applied in the app namespace but the Redwood components live in `redwood-system` (control plane IPs may be cluster-internal or in another namespace); (2) cluster DNS / egress to control plane IPs are blocked. Are your CNI egress rules scoped cluster-wide (Calico/Antrea?) or namespaced?

acme-devops: Using Calico, we enabled a global default deny by applying a policy in `prod` namespace only — we assumed namespace-scoped policies wouldn't touch `redwood-system`. But the agent pods in `prod` still fail.

Alex (Eng): Quick check — `redwood-agent` running in `prod` will still need outbound connectivity to: (a) cluster DNS (UDP 53), (b) control plane FQDNs/IPs (TCP 443), and (c) any metadata endpoints if you use cloud instance metadata. Try allowing egress to the control-plane CIDR and to DNS. Example minimal NetworkPolicy to allow agent egress: 

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-agent-egress-allow
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.42.0.0/16   # cluster pod/service CIDR (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

Priya (SRE): Also verify that DNS lookups from the agent succeed. Try: `kubectl -n prod exec -it <agent-pod> -- nslookup controller.redwood.internal` and `curl -v --resolve controller.redwood.internal:443:10.42.5.3 https://controller.redwood.internal/health` to test TLS. If `nslookup` times out, you likely blocked UDP 53 or egress to kube-dns.

acme-devops: Ran nslookup — it times out. `nslookup controller.redwood.internal` shows no response.

Daniel (Infra): If you have Calico default deny at the cluster level, serviceAccount/Namespace isolation can still block traffic (e.g., egress to ClusterIP DNS). For Calico, you can add a GlobalNetworkPolicy or a namespaced allow for `kube-dns` ClusterIP (usually in `kube-system`) and to the control-plane CIDR. Example allow to DNS ClusterIP: 

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-dns-egress
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.10/32   # kube-dns clusterIP (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

Lina (Support): If you can, capture a tcpdump from the agent pod to show whether UDP 53 or TCP 443 packets are leaving. If packets aren't leaving, it's NP/CNI blocking. If packets leave but no response, likely firewall/egress ACLs at infra level.

acme-devops: Ok we added two temporary NPs allowing UDP/53 to kube-dns IP and TCP/443 to the control-plane IP range. After that the agent logs show successful TLS handshake. 

```
2026-03-12T14:06:22Z info tls: handshake completed with controller.redwood.internal (10.42.5.3:443)
```

acme-devops: Verified API calls are back and latency is normal. :white_check_mark: Thanks for the quick help — we'll tighten rules and create scoped allowlists for the agent label.

Lina (Support): Great — glad that fixed it. Next steps we recommend: (1) create label-scoped egress allow policies for `app=redwood-agent`; (2) allow DNS (UDP 53) to kube-dns or add a DNS proxy that agent can use; (3) list control-plane IPs / FQDNs in your egress allowlist. If you want, we can share a policy bundle we use for Calico/Antrea.

ops-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-142 (private-connectivity). Assigned to Lina (Support).

Alex (Eng): Adding one more note — if you rely on node-local DNS or hostNetwork, update your NP accordingly. Also consider allowing kube-apiserver metadata if agent pulls instance metadata.

acme-devops: We'll follow up if we need the policy bundle. Appreciate the pointers!
